revision_notes: GSMA Intelligence data reported by Connecting Africa (Sept 2025 and May 2026) shows 4G population coverage at 57%, up from 42% in 2020, above the 48% cited from the 2024/25 Broadband Commission report. revision_notes: The cited A4AI figure dates from 2021 and could not be corroborated with a precise, current % of GNI per capita from ITU's 2024 ICT Price Basket report — the underlying country-level data tables were not extractable in this session. Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: World Bank/ITU data show individuals using the internet at 19.67% in 2024 (up from 18.97% in 2023), closely corroborated by GSMA's own 2024 estimate of about 17% unique mobile internet users. This conflicts with DataReportal's 30.5% (2025/26 reports), which appears to conflate broader mobile connections/broadband with internet use. Revised down from 3 (30-49%) to 2 (15-29%) on the better-corroborated ITU/World Bank/GSMA figures.

Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: PeeringDB and bgp.tools show KINIX with roughly 23 participating ASNs, including major global content networks (Meta, Cloudflare) and multiple national ISPs/operators (Vodacom Congo, Orange-affiliated networks), which goes beyond 'limited participation'. Revised from 3 to 4 (active IXP with moderate participation) on two corroborating, current registry sources.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: DataReportal/GSMA Intelligence report mobile connections at 56.9% of population (Oct 2025), which the original row used as a proxy for unique subscribers, but the variable requires unique-subscriber penetration and GSMA/DataReportal explicitly warn against treating connections as a unique-subscriber proxy given known multi-SIM prevalence in DRC. No verified unique-subscriber percentage was located this session. Left unchanged from 4 but flagged for human review rather than confirmed, since true unique-subscriber penetration is plausibly lower (possibly band 3, 40-54%).

Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted but no enforcement authority
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: the 2023 Digital Code establishes the Autorite de Protection des Donnees (APD, Arts 262-270), but the enabling Prime Ministerial decree has still not been adopted; a contested August 2024 ministerial order temporarily transferred APD functions to telecoms regulator ARPTIC. Legislation enacted but no dedicated enforcement authority is still an accurate description — code 3 confirmed with more current, corroborating sources.

Measured through proxies such as GitHub activity, Stack Overflow representation, local tech meetup groups, and developer surveys. Indicates the country's capacity to build and maintain digital systems locally.
Value Name: Emerging (small but growing community, <1,000 active developers)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: GitHub's Innovation Graph only reports developer metrics for DRC because it crosses GitHub's 100-unique-developer reporting threshold, and AfriLabs lists just one active hub (Kinshasa Digital Academy) in-country — both consistent with a small, emerging developer community, though an exact headcount could not be obtained this session. Code 2 (Emerging, <1,000 developers) retained on qualitative corroboration; the original generic GitHub topics-page source replaced with more authoritative GitHub and AfriLabs sources.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
